reportSubtitle: Traffic Quality Improving, Fixed the CPA Target
summary:
Traffic quality improved last week — CPC dropped 22% ($7.63 to $5.92), CTR climbed to 10.61%, and click volume ticked up slightly. Competitive pressure from the new local entrants eased a bit in the auction.

Conversions are back at 1 for the week though, which is the signal I've been watching. I dug into the account and found a propbably issue: a change back on Apr 4 dropped the Target CPA from $100 to the $80 campaign default, even though actual cost per conversion has been running around $153 over the last 30 days. Smart Bidding was walking away from auctions because it couldn't hit a target that was roughly half of reality. I reverted that today and added 4 high-intent exact match keywords to give the algorithm better signals to work with.

metrics.label: Ad Spend
metrics.note: Down $30 from the previous week. Still budget-limited at $40/day but Smart Bidding held back on some days.

metrics.label: Conversions
metrics.note: Flat at 1 for a second week. Expecting recovery now that the CPA target is realistic.

metrics.label: Cost per Conversion
metrics.note: Down from $320 last week but still well above our $153 30-day average.

metrics.label: CTR
metrics.note: Up from 9.17%. Ads are resonating — people are clicking when they see us.

funnel.title: Ad-to-Booking Funnel
funnel.notes: 'Bartenders for hire' broad match still drove 97% of spend ($282 of $290) — concentration risk persists.

charts.title: Weekly Trend — CPC Cooled Off This Week
Spend by Keyword — The Concentration Problem

findings.title: The Algorithm Likely Backed Off
findings.description: Over the past 30 days actual cost per conversion has been $153 — Smart Bidding couldn't hit $80, so it pulled back on bids and impression share. That aligns with what we saw: strong CTR and clean search terms, but suppressed volume.

findings.title: Competitive CPC Pressure Eased This Week
findings.description: Avg CPC dropped from $7.63 to $5.92 — a 22% decrease. Either some of last week's new local entrants (Velvet Alchemy, Bad Rabbit Caravan, etc.) pulled back on bids, or google views our ads as more relevant. CTR of 10.61% suggests the latter is at least partly true.

findings.title: Broad Match Concentration Is Still 97%
findings.description: 'Bartenders for hire' broad match continues to eat 97% of spend ($282 of $290). Phrase match keywords got basically zero spend again this week. TWe've been tracking this long enough to do something about it.

actions.title: Reverted Target CPA to $100 at the Ad Group Level
actions.description: Set a $100 Target CPA override on the Bar Catering ad group so Smart Bidding stops optimizing to the unrealistic $80 default. This gives the algorithm room to bid in auctions where it thinks a conversion is likely to come in above $80.

actions.title: Added 4 Exact Match High-Intent Keywords
actions.description: Added [hire a bartender], [bartender for hire], [event bartending], and [bartender rental for party] as exact match. These are all search terms that have been converting or showing high intent in search term reports. Exact match gives Smart Bidding a cleaner signal than relying on one broad match keyword.

nextSteps: Watch for conversion recovery over the next 7-10 days as Smart Bidding re-learns against the $100 target.
Track impression volume on the new exact match keywords — 'Pending Under review' status should clear within 24 hours.
